scenario: Monday of the cycle's final week, with the week already precise. The athlete says Friday's gym is closed for maintenance that day and asks where Friday's session goes instead.
given: This week's five sessions are already written: Monday's full-body strength, Tuesday's 8km easy run at 6:30-7:00/km, Thursday's seven-repetition threshold session at 5:55/km, Friday's upper-body strength, and Sunday's 15km long run at 6:35-7:05/km.
The athlete's stated reason is that the gym they use for Friday's session is closed for maintenance that one day. They have said nothing else about the week.
Friday's session is upper-body work; Sunday's session is a long run.
Nothing about availability on any other day, recovery, or the cycle's goal has changed.

expected.conclusion: The closed gym touches Friday's session and nothing else, so only Friday moves -- to Saturday, which is otherwise open and does not compete with Sunday's long run the way lower-body work would. Monday's session, Tuesday's pace, Thursday's prescription and Sunday's long run stay exactly as they were already written; the answer is one line, not a new week.
must_state: That Friday's upper-body session is what moves, and that it moves to Saturday.
Why Saturday works: it is otherwise open and, being upper-body work, does not compete with Sunday's long run the way moving lower-body work there would.

That every other already-committed session this week -- Monday's strength, Tuesday's easy run, Thursday's threshold session, Sunday's long run -- keeps exactly the date and prescription it already had.
That the reason for the move is the stated gym closure, not a broader look at the week.
must_not_state: Any changed pace, load, or distance for Monday's, Tuesday's, Thursday's, or Sunday's sessions.
A restated or re-explained version of a session the gym closure does not touch, as if the whole week were being reissued.
A different day for Friday's session than Saturday, or a second session added elsewhere to absorb the disruption.
That the week's overall structure, density, or the cycle's direction is being reconsidered because of one closed gym.

fails_if: The answer moves Friday's session and also restates, re-paces, or reorders one or more of the other four sessions the gym closure does not touch -- the whole-week rewrite this case exists to catch.
The answer leaves Friday's session where it is and tells the athlete to find another gym, refusing a request the evidence supports.
The answer moves the session somewhere that competes with Sunday's long run, or does not say why Saturday avoids that.
The answer turns one day's fix into a broader review of the week's density, loads, or the cycle's progress.
